verification_report.summary: The complete staged manuscript passes the sequential audit, conditional on the exact comparison, subsolution and Gauduchon premises in item 5 and the other stipulated internal inputs. [DP04, Theorem 3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0105176v2) supplies decreasing regularization with a resolved smooth remainder; its application to the closed current dd^c u allows a nonclosed smooth lower bound. The resolution proves semipositive bigness upstairs, preserves the Lp density class, and permits the stated descent. The normalization constants and fixed barrier translates give the required uniform estimates. Disjoint contact partitions avoid input-count factors, and every Monge–Ampere limit uses uniformly locally bounded monotone sequences off the analytic pole set. In the zero-exponent argument, the Gauduchon trace and weighted subsolutions bound c_j above and away from zero and control the ordinary singularity type; the artificial fixed positive exponent correctly identifies the envelope limits. Scalar uniqueness follows, while zero-exponent potential uniqueness is not asserted. [BGL25, published Theorems 4.6–4.7](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42543-025-00105-2) matches the attribution. No semipositivity or closedness of theta, BMP, PVP, or general-measure existence is assumed or inferred. Finite mass is concluded only for the constructed solutions.
